correctness.rationale: The claim is a finite statement on all 81 ternary words of length four. The verifier constructs one-deletion shadows by two independent definitions, builds the exact compatibility graph, and proves the optimum twice: maximal-clique enumeration reaches size 11 with six equality cases, while an independent increasing-vertex fixed-size enumeration counts six 11-cliques and zero 12-cliques. The structural core, six-cycle parametrization, declared symmetry orbit, and 23-of-27 coverage count are recomputed from those six equality cases. The result makes no extrapolation beyond this finite domain.

value.rationale: Alphabet size three is the smallest nonbinary odd alphabet and length four is the canonical finite regime in which sharp even-alphabet single-deletion theory is known. The contribution is not merely a recomputed number: it gives a complete natural equality-case classification, a nine-word forced core, a six-cycle parametrization of all optima, one symmetry orbit, and a non-perfect coverage profile. These structural facts make the instance a reusable benchmark and base case for the odd-alphabet length-four problem.
